propositions: Cloud identifies users by opaque accountId while Data Center identifies them by name, creating a contract gap in assignee resolution that leaks into OutboundMapper and transport payloads.

PR #120 hardcoded is_account_id=False and consulted an unset _assignee_resolver attribute, making the authoritative branch unreachable and causing DC to permanently return authoritative=False, which drives assignee-diff churn on every sync pass.

A UserIdentityModel Protocol with resolve() and to_payload() methods must normalize the 3-state (value, authoritative, is_account_id) tuple, with AccountIdIdentity for Cloud (existing behavior) and NameIdentity for DC (real lookup against user-search endpoint).

NameIdentity must perform a real lookup against DC's user-search endpoint and inject the resolver explicitly at construction, not via getattr, so it can return authoritative=True and converge the diff.

The implementation must pass a shared parameterized contract test covering all three resolution states (empty, converged, different identity) and must assert DC returns authoritative=True for resolvable assignees to prevent churn regression.
An unresolvable assignee must raise BackendAssigneeNotFoundError rather than silently returning a non-authoritative value, and Cloud's existing pinned behavior from J1 must remain unchanged.
